protocol.question: Does substituting a language-matched historical scoring profile improve independent-key recovery over the modern-English baseline and deliberately mismatched historical profiles at the same solver budget?
protocol.registration: This local protocol was fixed before the recovery outcomes were inspected. It is not an external preregistration or a blind benchmark.

selection.rule: Use passages 2 and 3 from each of the three existing author-disjoint sources. Exclude every first passage before any solver run because it contains edition front matter or introductory prose. No selection uses recovery results.

excluded.reason: Begins with edition and publisher front matter mixed with the work's dedication.
An editor discusses a 1912 edition and changes to spelling; this is not Machiavelli's dramatic prose.
Introductory third-person prose about Cicero and Catiline, rather than the selected orations; authorship and period are not established by the existing fixture.

sourceAuthors.brantome-dames-galantes: Pierre de Bourdeille, seigneur de Brantome

protocol.normalization: Use the profile builder's accent/ligature folds and uppercase A-Z only; remove word boundaries, punctuation and digits. Preserve I/J and U/V distinctions. Score the full normalized selected passage, without truncation. This is lossy editorial normalization, not diplomatic transcription.

cipher.keySeedRule: research-splits.seedFor('test', protocol.id + ':' + passage.id + ':replicate-' + replicate, 'key'), using the existing reserved test seed range. Assert unique seeds and different ciphertexts across all 30 cases.
cipher.keyVisibility: Public ground truth is used to construct fixtures and calculate errors after search. Solvers receive only symbol tokens, an empty locked key, the declared budget and one scoring function. No shared code pool, cribs or known-key initialization.

protocol.pairing: Every scorer sees exactly the same ciphertext, search seed and budget within a case and solver. Beam search is deterministic and does not use the search seed. Five replicas vary independently drawn keys as well as annealing seeds; they do not isolate search-seed variance from key variance. Budgets match within each solver, not between different algorithms.
protocol.outcome: Score only the top candidate returned by each solver. Primary: plaintext Levenshtein edit distance divided by expected plaintext length. Also report positional character error, observed-symbol key error and exact plaintext recovery. Lower error is better. Compare matched minus baseline and matched minus the mean of BOTH mismatched profiles within each case; negative paired differences favor the matched model. Publish every run, per-language and per-passage summaries, and wins/ties/losses. No best-seed selection, hyperparameter tuning, significance claim or success threshold.
protocol.mismatchControl: Run every historical profile on every case. The one matching the source LANGUAGE is the matched condition; the other two are separate deliberately mismatched controls. This is not necessarily an exact period match, particularly Dante's profile applied to Machiavelli.
protocol.fixedModelScope: Use the shipped profile counts, pruning, frequency penalty and solver proposal/temperature schedule without retraining or rescaling. This tests the existing model substitutions as implemented, not the isolated causal effect of historical spelling or equalized model capacity. A matched modern-language baseline is not available here.

limits: Six public passages, two from each of three works/authors. Thirty independently keyed cases are not thirty independent documents; variants remain grouped by source.
The first passage of every existing author-disjoint source is excluded for front-matter/introductory contamination before outcomes. Existing v2 files and their earlier results are preserved.
Author and work disjointness is checked against explicit source identities and author metadata, not claimed for every possible unrecorded textual borrowing or edition editor.

Matched means language-matched, not necessarily period-, genre- or orthography-matched. The Italian edition states that some spellings were modernized; removing its preface does not undo those editorial decisions.
Both mismatched historical models are run separately on each case. Their pooled mean uses two runs per case; paired comparisons first average those two controls within each case.
Five fixed paired key/search seeds are all published. They vary keys as well as annealing randomness, and are not an isolated estimate of search-seed variance.

Scores, corpus sizes, pruning and unseen-gram floors differ among models. No cross-model likelihood comparison or temperature rescaling is performed; the outcome is externally measured recovery error.

The shipped annealer still uses an English-weighted initial proposal distribution and the beam uses its shipped extension order. Both are held fixed across scorers. These are implementation-specific model substitutions, not a general comparison of language models.
No matched modern French, Italian or Latin baseline is available, so this experiment cannot identify a benefit of historical spelling separately from language matching.
Only clean A-Z letter-homophone ciphertexts are tested. No numerical segmentation, nulls, word codes, transcription ambiguity or authentic unknown historical cipher is recovered here.

Replay needs identical inputs, scorer/solver builds and JavaScript execution behavior. Node/V8/platform/architecture/locale and input hashes are recorded. Cross-engine search paths are not promised to match.

The check command audits provenance, pairing, model identity, complete matrix and arithmetic without rerunning search. Replay reruns every search and demands exact results except runtime; it does not accept a broad per-item error tolerance.
No score-based cherry-picking, best-of-seed reporting, inferential significance or general decipherment-accuracy claim is supported by this bounded experiment.
